trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going to (8,9) would leave both cell (7,9) and cell (9,9) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going to (8,7), the next 9 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,7) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes to (7,8).
Cell (7,9) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (8,9).
Going to (8,7), the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,7). So the line goes to (9,6).
I can't rule out to (8,6) or to (9,5) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (8,6).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to number 5, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (3,2), the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,1). So my guess (to (8,6) from cell (9,6)) was wrong, so the line must go to (9,5).
The line must go to (8,5): to (9,3) is number 9, which comes later.
Going to (7,5) would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (8,3) would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (8,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (8,7).

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,9).

Going to (3,12) would cut off the top-right corner (6 cells). So the line goes to (4,13).

Going to (2,5), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,3).
Cell (1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,2).
Going to (3,2), the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,1). So the line goes to (2,3).
The line must go to (2,5): to (3,3) is number 7, which comes later.
Going to (3,5) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,6).
Going to (3,6) would leave both cell (3,7) and cell (4,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (2,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (3,7).
Cell (4,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,5).
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.

Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (3,1).
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,5).
Cell (8,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (9,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
